threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use 'the tube' like it's your lifeline, but watch out—most of us just cycle or walk everywhere around here.
Last week on the 59, I saw a guy offer his last slice of pizza to a sleeping woman. She woke up, took it, and went back to sleep. London’s night buses are wild.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a family of ducks crossing Hermannstraße during rush hour, completely unfazed by the chaos around them. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you witness spontaneous street parties erupting any night of the week, complete with DJs and feasting locals. It's alive!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local will tell you the shortcut to avoid 16th St BART when the train's down—taking the alleys to catch the 14 instead.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy singing opera on the 6 bus while the engine rattled through the Tenderloin. Just a regular Thursday in SF, you know?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's only about Gaudí. They miss the quiet plazas where locals gather after work, sipping vermut and chatting till late.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their hesitation at the ‘bocadillos’ counter, still trying to figure out the right filling combinations.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Clapton is part of Hackney, not a whole other vibe. That and asking for directions instead of just sharing the pavement.
Last night on the 35, a guy pulled out a full chess set and started a game with a stranger. Only in Brixton, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The sound of an old lady yelling at her cat in the morning instead of church bells really hit home. This place has its own rhythm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you spot a spontaneous outdoor gallery pop up on a street corner while sipping a late-night kebab. It's an art exhibit and snack bar all in one.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for BART's small talk—'mornings are for silence' is a common mantra, especially after delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon casually riding the 47 last week, just strutting down the aisle like it owned the place. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for sipping sangria, but locals know they're really for kids playing futbol until sundown.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still look up at the buildings instead of walking with their heads down, lost in their phones.
